subject.title: feat(control-ui): render Mermaid code fences in webchat

question: Should OpenClaw core accept built-in Mermaid SVG rendering for untrusted webchat markdown, and under what sanitizer/dependency constraints?
rationale: The feature is user-visible and useful, but it expands browser rendering and sanitizer behavior for model/chat content and adds workspace dependency resolution surface; automation cannot decide that product/security tradeoff.

options.title: Require a current-main port with security proof
options.body: Move the implementation to the current markdown-it webchat path, remove or justify the override, and require browser proof for streaming, malformed, sanitizer-sensitive, and theme cases before merge.

options.title: Approve built-in Mermaid as a sponsored feature
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the sanitizer and dependency surface after reviewing current-head proof and focused tests.

options.title: Close and ask for a fresh branch
options.body: If reviving this branch is more expensive than the feature, close it and invite a narrow replacement against current main.

recommendation.title: Require a current-main port with security proof
recommendation.body: Move the implementation to the current markdown-it webchat path, remove or justify the override, and require browser proof for streaming, malformed, sanitizer-sensitive, and theme cases before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc appears in adjacent current-main commit metadata and was subscribed on the PR for review routing, making him the best available decision owner from the observed signals.
